method_note: Ground truth is authored here first; the claim documents in data/claims/ are rendered from it in phase 2, and eval/verify_corpus.py asserts the rendered documents still contain exactly what is declared here. The application never reads this file (CLAUDE.md 2.8). 'facts' holds canonical normalised values - surface variation (date formats, currency formats, field labels) is added at render time and is declared under near_misses, not here.

field_glossary.incident_time: time of day of the incident, 24h
field_glossary.intimation_date: date the claim was intimated to the insurer, drives C-06
field_glossary.theft_discovery_date: date the theft was discovered, drives C-07
field_glossary.fir_date: date the First Information Report was lodged, drives C-07
field_glossary.document_submission_date: date the document set was submitted, drives C-08
field_glossary.claim_amount: amount claimed in rupees, drives C-04
field_glossary.insured_declared_value: IDV from the policy schedule in rupees, drives C-04
field_glossary.engine_capacity_cc: engine capacity, drives C-05 band selection
field_glossary.driving_licence_expiry_date: drives C-11; must be present on every accident claim form or C-11 returns UNKNOWN
field_glossary.damage_location: point of impact as reported, compared against the repair estimate for C-16

cases.title: Routine own-damage claim, nothing wrong

facts.incident_summary: Sideswiped by an auto-rickshaw changing lanes; damage to the front-left fender and headlamp.

cases.why_this_case_exists: The baseline. A clean claim must come back clean with no manufactured concerns; a regression here is the most damaging failure mode we have.

cases.title: Theft claim, FIR present and timely

facts.incident_location: Apartment basement parking, 4th Block Jayanagar, Bengaluru
facts.incident_summary: Vehicle found missing from the basement parking bay on the morning of 11 February.

near_misses.what_differed: claim amount of Rs 72,000 is exactly equal to the IDV of Rs 72,000
near_misses.why_dismissed: C-04 caps a claim that exceeds the IDV; a claim equal to it is within the limit

cases.why_this_case_exists: The second clean case, and a boundary test: total loss settled at exactly the IDV must not trip the cap in C-04.

cases.title: Clean but superficially odd - large claim, incident at 02:35

facts.incident_summary: Struck stray cattle on the highway while returning from Kilpauk Medical College Hospital after a family emergency; front end and radiator damaged.

near_misses.what_differed: incident occurred at 02:35, outside normal driving hours
near_misses.why_dismissed: no clause in the policy restricts the time of day at which cover applies

near_misses.what_differed: claim of Rs 2,94,750 is large in absolute terms
near_misses.why_dismissed: well within the IDV of Rs 12,80,000 and consistent with the estimate line items

cases.why_this_case_exists: Proves the system does not flag on suspicion. A night-time incident and a large amount are the two things a naive reviewer would escalate, and neither breaches any clause.

cases.title: Incident date conflicts between claim form and FIR, and the conflict decides the intimation window

facts.incident_location: Ring Road near Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi
facts.incident_summary: Rear-ended at a signal by a light commercial vehicle; rear bumper, boot lid and tail lamp damaged.
facts.police_station: Lajpat Nagar Police Station, New Delhi

planted.detail: claim form states 14 March 2026, the FIR states 12 March 2026
planted.consequence: The intimation on 15 March is within the 48 hour window in C-06 if the incident was on the 14th and outside it if the incident was on the 12th, so the disagreement decides whether a policy condition was breached. It cannot be resolved from the packet.

near_misses.what_differed: DL-8C-AF-3092 on the claim form, DL8CAF3092 on the repair estimate
the intimation window check has a contradicted input
near_misses.why_dismissed: C-06 must return UNKNOWN rather than choosing one of the two dates; emitting a cited POLICY_DEVIATION from a disputed value would be a false finding wearing a citation

cases.why_this_case_exists: The signature contradiction case. It also tests that a deterministic check refuses to evaluate on a disputed input instead of silently picking a side.

cases.title: Theft claim with no FIR in the packet

facts.incident_location: Street parking outside 12 Shivranjani Cross Road, Ahmedabad
facts.incident_summary: Vehicle parked on the street overnight and found missing early the next morning.

planted.detail: C-10 requires a copy of the First Information Report for a theft claim and no FIR is present in the packet
planted.consequence: Blocking incompleteness, so the review requests the FIR by name rather than assessing the claim on an incomplete packet.

near_misses.what_differed: the FIR window check has no fir_date to evaluate
near_misses.why_dismissed: the absent FIR is already reported once by C-10; C-07 must return UNKNOWN rather than reporting the same absence a second time as a missed deadline

cases.why_this_case_exists: Absence is a finding, and it must be reported exactly once. Double-reporting one absence as both a missing document and a missed deadline is a real failure mode.

cases.title: Repair estimate bills rear-end parts against a front-impact narrative

facts.incident_location: Mumbai-Bengaluru Highway service road, Warje, Pune
facts.incident_summary: Swerved to avoid a stopped vehicle and struck the concrete road divider head on; the front of the car took the impact.

planted.detail: the claim form and customer narrative both describe a front impact, while the repair estimate bills a rear bumper assembly and a rear tail lamp
planted.consequence: The documents disagree about which part of the vehicle was damaged, which cannot be resolved from the packet and requires a surveyor.

planted.detail: C-16 requires the repair estimate to relate to the damage reported; rear-end parts billed against a front impact do not
planted.consequence: A model-proposed clause application, capped at material by ADR-001, so it escalates rather than rejecting.

cases.why_this_case_exists: One fact produces two findings of different classes that must not be collapsed: the documents disagreeing with each other is a CONTRADICTION, the estimate not relating to the reported damage is a POLICY_DEVIATION under C-16. Both are true and they say different things to the investigator.

cases.title: Claim amount exceeds the insured declared value

facts.incident_summary: Hit from the side by a car jumping a signal; extensive damage across both left-side doors, the B-pillar and the left suspension.

planted.detail: claimed Rs 2,12,000 against an IDV of Rs 1,85,000, a ratio of 1.15
planted.consequence: Below the 1.5 escalation ratio, so the excess is arithmetic rather than a defect: settlement is capped at the IDV and the report shows claimed Rs 2,12,000, payable Rs 1,85,000, difference Rs 27,000.

near_misses.what_differed: Rs. 2,12,000 on the claim form, 212000.00 as the estimate total

cases.why_this_case_exists: The only case that reaches APPROVE_CAPPED, and it tests that an ordinary excess stays informational rather than escalating. The 1.5 ratio exists so that a claim at three times the IDV is treated as a different event; this claim is deliberately below it.

cases.title: Driving licence had expired before the incident, with a commercial-use concern alongside it

facts.incident_summary: Collided with a stationary tempo while pulling out; front right quarter panel and headlamp damaged.

estimate_lines.description: Front bumper assembly - repair and refinish

planted.detail: licence expired 31 January 2026, incident occurred 8 April 2026
planted.consequence: A machine-checkable exclusion on a date comparison, so it is permitted to be blocking and the recommendation is REJECT with C-11 quoted.

planted.detail: the customer narrative describes dropping off a paying passenger before the incident, which C-13 excludes
planted.consequence: A model proposal, capped at material. It is reported as a finding but does not drive the recommendation, which is already determined by the deterministic exclusion above it in the ordering.

cases.why_this_case_exists: The only case that reaches REJECT, and it demonstrates the authority split in one packet: a deterministic date comparison rejects, while a model-proposed exclusion that a human might consider more serious is reported but subordinate. A finding that does not drive the recommendation must still appear in the report.

cases.title: Clean claim buried under near-misses

facts.incident_location: Faizabad Road near Indira Nagar, Lucknow
facts.incident_summary: A two-wheeler collided with the rear left of the car at a junction; rear left door and quarter panel dented.

estimate_lines.description: Rear left door - repair and refinish
Rear left quarter panel - dent removal

near_misses.what_differed: UP-32-DN-6647 on the claim form, UP32DN6647 on the repair estimate, U.P. 32 DN 6647 in the FIR
12/02/2026 on the claim form, 12-Feb-2026 on the estimate, February 12, 2026 in the narrative
near_misses.why_dismissed: identical date after parsing; the day-first format is unambiguous here because 12 is a valid month and day but all three sources agree once parsed

near_misses.what_differed: Rs. 64,900 on the claim form, 64900.00 as the estimate total
estimate line items sum to Rs 55,000 while the estimate total reads Rs 64,900
near_misses.why_dismissed: the difference is 18 percent GST stated on the estimate; the totals reconcile once tax is accounted for

near_misses.what_differed: Rajesh Kumar Singh on the claim form, R. K. Singh in the FIR, Rajesh K Singh on the estimate
near_misses.why_dismissed: same person after name normalisation of initials

near_misses.what_differed: 18:30 on the claim form, approximately 6.30 in the evening in the narrative
near_misses.why_dismissed: identical time after normalisation; the narrative is approximate by its own wording

near_misses.what_differed: the FIR was lodged on 14 February, two days after the incident on the 12th
near_misses.why_dismissed: C-07 imposes a 72 hour FIR window on theft claims only; no clause imposes an FIR deadline on an own-damage claim, and this FIR is in any case within 72 hours

cases.why_this_case_exists: The calibration case. Seven things look wrong and none of them are. Every one must appear under considered and dismissed with its reason, and none may appear as a finding. If a near-miss leaks into findings as informational, the clean cases stop looking clean and the calibration story is gone.

cases.title: Held-out theft case - authored after code freeze
cases.why_this_case_exists: Written after the detection code is frozen and never used during development, so its result is a genuine held-out measurement. The result is recorded honestly in the README including if it fails, because a caught miss with an explanation is worth more than a suspiciously perfect run.
